clue.text: Musical opener for warm-up man at conference?

definitions.meaning: the title of a Sondheim stage show set in ancient Rome

definitions.text: opener for warm-up man at conference?
definitions.meaning: a stand-up's stock first line about something amusing on the way in, with a forum being a conference

explanation.surface: Asks what tune or line a comedian warming up a conference audience would start with.
explanation.walkthrough: The stage show's title is also the classic comic's opening gambit, with 'forum' doubling as a meeting place, hence 'conference'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of the 1962 Sondheim stage show, and also the stock opening of a comedian's anecdote.

clue.text: Unusually expressive person losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word for person drops its first letter

parts.note: in legal language a party is a person involved in a case or contract

explanation.surface: Describes someone flamboyant who has lost their composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone affectedly artistic is showily, unusually expressive in manner and dress.

clue.text: Delays human trafficking? Absolutely

indicators.note: trafficking means dealing in and moving things about, so the letters of the two words are moved around

explanation.surface: Condemns delays in tackling people-smuggling, with a firm 'absolutely' in agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trafficking' rearranges DELAYS HUMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without shame means doing it openly and completely, so the adverb can stand for absolutely.

clue.text: Sporting item suggesting square leg?

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: Sounds like a cricket question: square leg is a fielding position beside the batter.
explanation.walkthrough: Square leg is a cricket fielding position, but here 'square' gives NINE and 'leg' gives PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the skittles set up in the bowling game of the same name, so a piece of sports kit.

clue.text: "Open the claret, me? Not so" — its landlord might say?

definitions.text: "Open the claret, me? Not so" — its landlord might say?

indicators.note: not so means not in this form, so the letters of the quoted request are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teetotal landlord refuses to uncork the wine for a guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so' rearranges OPEN THE CLARET ME, and the whole clue is what the keeper of such a dry establishment would say.
explanation.definitionFit: Such an establishment served no alcohol, so its keeper would refuse to open wine.

clue.text: Jailed? Old fellow gets prison sentence with moments to spare

parts.note: the nick is British slang for prison, so being in it means jailed
doing time means serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A jailed old man receives a sentence just before the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the nick' is British slang for prison or a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means only just before it would be too late, so with barely any moments to spare.

clue.text: Response from dog after cornering the old soaring bird

indicators.note: cornering means trapping, so the dog's response closes around the other letters

parts.note: a dog may respond with a growl

indicators.note: soaring means rising, and in a down entry the old form of the is read upwards

parts.note: ye is an old way of writing the

explanation.surface: A dog growls after trapping an elderly bird that had been flying high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soaring' turns YE upwards to EY, which the growl corners.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large northern species of owl, so a type of bird.

clue.text: Bog in space between hills mostly retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the shortened word is read backwards
mostly means all but the last letter of the valley word

parts.note: a vale is a valley

explanation.surface: Something swampy in a valley is withdrawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts VALE to VAL; 'retreating' reverses it. 'Bog' is British slang for a toilet, not a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a toilet, the second short for lavatory.

clue.text: Floral tribute certain to be overlooked by the rest

indicators.note: overlooked means ignored, so the word for certain is left out

parts.note: leisure is time for rest
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A wreath of flowers that is sure to be ignored by everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be overlooked' removes SURE from LEISURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hawaiian garland of flowers is placed round a visitor's neck as a welcome tribute.

clue.text: Sketch-writer setting it unexpectedly beneath Vatican City

indicators.note: beneath places the shuffled letters below the city's code in this down entry

parts.note: V is the international vehicle code for Vatican City

indicators.note: unexpectedly means in an unforeseen way, so the letters of the two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A satirist sets a sketch, surprisingly, in the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges SETTING IT to IGNETTIST, which goes 'beneath' V.
explanation.definitionFit: A vignette is a short descriptive sketch, so its writer is a sketch-writer.

clue.text: Endless yarn interrupted by a US storyteller

indicators.note: interrupted by means the shortened word is broken open by a letter
endless means the string word loses its last letter

parts.note: twine is a kind of yarn or string

explanation.surface: An American storyteller's never-ending yarn gets cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a story, but it is string: TWINE, 'Endless' to TWIN, with A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain, author of Tom Sawyer, is the best-known American storyteller by that pen name.

clue.text: Indistinctly mentioning money and the production of counterfeit money

parts.note: uttering is the legal term for passing forged money or documents

explanation.surface: Someone mumbles about cash and forgery.
explanation.walkthrough: In law, to utter is to put forged notes or documents into circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking under the breath is a way of mentioning something unclearly, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 1
Wasted a month with Eniac — showing early form of this?

definitions.text: Wasted a month with Eniac — showing early form of this?

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so the letters of the phrase are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone squanders a month on a vintage computer, a symptom of obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' rearranges A MONTH ENIAC. ENIAC was one of the first electronic computers, so lavishing a month on it suggests an early case of gadget obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: It means an obsessive enthusiasm for technology, which spending weeks on an early computer would show.

clue.text: A flogger, though not necessarily a dominatrix

definitions.text: A flogger, though not necessarily a dominatrix

parts.words: A flogger, though not necessarily a dominatrix
parts.note: to flog is British slang for to sell, so a female flogger is a seller, not one who whips

explanation.surface: A whip-wielder who is not, after all, in the bondage trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' is British slang for sell, so the woman is a seller rather than a whipper.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who sells goods for a living is a female flogger in the slang sense.

clue.text: Military supplies rejected a popular pungent gas

parts.note: ammo is short for ammunition

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the two short pieces are read backwards

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: An army turns down a well-liked chemical weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns A IN into NIA.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the sharp-smelling compound of nitrogen and hydrogen, a gas with a strong odour.

clue.text: Criminal's heart skipping a beat, ultimately, in pursuit of Channel Islands criminal

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following, so the last letter comes after the islands' abbreviation
skipping means leaving out, so the single letter is dropped
heart means the middle, so the villain word loses its outer letters

parts.note: a villain is a criminal

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word beat

explanation.surface: A villain's heart misses a beat while chasing a crook from Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' cuts VILLAIN to ILLAI and 'skipping' drops A to leave ILLI. The Channel Islands, including Jersey and Guernsey, lie off France.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden by law is unlawful, a direct synonym for criminal.

clue.text: Stop me backing one Conservative over all the district

parts.note: end means stop

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word me is read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A plea to halt a Tory canvassing the whole area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease or species found regularly throughout a particular area is described this way; the adjective is used predicatively here.

clue.text: Justice League conflated with Iron Man's premiere? One of Marvel's weapons

indicators.note: premiere means the first showing, so the first letter of Man is taken

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for Justice, a judge's title

indicators.note: conflated means merged together, so the letters gathered are mixed up

explanation.surface: Superhero teams get mixed up in a film's opening night, naming a comic-book weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conflated' rearranges J, L, IRON and M. It is Thor's hammer in Marvel comics and films.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the hammer wielded by Thor, so one of the weapons in the Marvel universe.

clue.text: I'm working in Greek island in traditional costumes

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the island's name

parts.note: Kos is an island in the Dodecanese
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A worker on a Greek island is dressed in traditional garb.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the traditional Japanese robes, worn as national costume.

clue.text: Demonstrates support during endless disorder

indicators.note: during means within, so the support goes inside the shortened word
endless means the disorder word loses its last letter

parts.note: a mess is disorder
an arch is a supporting structure

explanation.surface: Protesters show their backing amid ongoing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts MESS to MES.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest by walking in procession is to demonstrate, so the verbs match in sense and form.

clue.text: See 1
Time to contribute to extra quantity of information

indicators.note: to contribute to means to go into, so the letter for time is put inside

parts.note: in cricket a bye is an extra, a run scored without the batter hitting the ball

explanation.surface: Someone needs time to add more to a pile of data.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an extra is a run not scored off the bat; a bye is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing it is a unit of data, usually eight bits, so a quantity of information.

clue.text: Italian futurist represented time in art

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Italian modernist depicted time in his painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges TIME IN ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Filippo Tommaso Marinetti wrote the 1909 Futurist Manifesto, founding the Italian movement.

clue.text: Theatre people seen around this?

indicators.note: seen around means the letters can be spotted straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Asks where you might spot actors.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'theatRE People', and the answer is itself a word for a theatre company.
explanation.definitionFit: A repertory company is a troupe of theatre people performing a series of plays.

clue.text: Convenient limits to heresy

parts.note: the limits of the word heresy are its first letter and its last letter

explanation.surface: Suggests that limits on heresy are merely a matter of convenience.
explanation.walkthrough: The limits of 'heresy' are H and Y; written out in full, with the 'and', they spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easy to use or close at hand is useful and convenient.

clue.text: Sleep is a good tip

definitions.meaning: in horse racing the tipster's most confident selection of the day

explanation.surface: Advice that rest is the best tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a short sleep, and in racing it is the tipster's best bet.

clue.text: Smart car towing fish is a form of wheeled transport

indicators.note: towing means pulling along behind, so the fish follows the car

parts.note: a Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce, a smart car
skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A posh car tows a fish trailer, a curious way to travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' points to the small Smart car brand, but here it means posh: a Roller is a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a boot fitted with wheels, so one way of getting about on wheels.
